paragraphs: The ScholarPredict project aims to develop a data-driven machine learning system for predicting academic performance categories of students using the Random Forest algorithm.
bullets: Primary Objective: Build an accurate and interpretable ensemble classification model that identifies students at risk early in the semester.
- Cleaned student dataset with attributes like attendance, internal assessment marks, assignments, previous grades, study hours, extracurricular activities.
- Used preprocessing techniques including missing-value imputation, categorical encoding, feature scaling, and class balancing using SMOTE.
- Divided data into training and testing sets for model development.
- Built a large number of decision trees on random subsets of the data and features to make predictions.
- Final category determined by majority voting across all trees.
- Evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and confusion matrix.
- Hyperparameter tuning with cross-validation improved results.
- Feature-importance analysis explained which attributes contributed most to each prediction.
- Compared against Decision Tree and Logistic Regression baselines for performance evaluation.
- Mentor dashboards, personalized study recommendations, dropout risk detection, institutional performance analysis.
